title: Compliance One-Pager (Draft) — Encryption & Key Management (KMS/HSM)
content:
Purpose
This one-pager provides customer-facing, RFP-ready language describing how Redwood Inference protects data in transit and at rest, how encryption keys are managed (including KMS/HSM options), and how encryption-related controls tie into logging and auditability across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Status / drafting notes (internal)
- Draft intended for Security/GRC + Solutions Engineering review. Do not send externally until moved to “Final” and linked from the Enablement Kit index.
- Do not promise roadmap items. If a prospect requests a capability not listed here (e.g., customer-managed keys for Hosted, special HSM constraints, or bespoke crypto modules), escalate via the questionnaire exceptions policy.

Executive summary (customer-facing)
Redwood Inference uses industry-standard encryption to protect customer data:
- In transit: TLS is used for API and console traffic; internal service-to-service communication is encrypted.
- At rest: Persistent storage is encrypted using cloud-provider encryption mechanisms; encryption is applied to applicable databases and backups.
- Key management: Key storage and rotation are handled using managed key management services (KMS) appropriate to the deployment model; for Private deployments, customers can use their own KMS/HSM controls within their environment.
- Auditability: Access and configuration changes are logged and can be integrated with customer audit programs (details vary by deployment mode).

Scope and definitions (customer-facing)
- “Customer data” may include prompts, completions, uploaded documents (if applicable), embeddings, and operational metadata (e.g., request identifiers). The precise set of stored data depends on product configuration and selected deployment mode.
- “At rest” refers to data stored on persistent media (e.g., databases, object storage, snapshots/backups). It does not typically include ephemeral processing memory required to run inference.
- Encryption is one component of security; access controls, network isolation, monitoring, and incident response are also part of Redwood’s security program.

1) Encryption in transit
Customer-facing endpoints
- Hosted API / Console: HTTPS using TLS (minimum versions and ciphers follow modern best practices and are periodically reviewed).
- Dedicated: Same API/Console interface with encrypted transport; network paths and endpoints are provisioned per customer configuration.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Traffic between customer clients and Redwood services can be constrained to private networking options and is encrypted in transit.

Internal communications
- Service-to-service traffic within Redwood-managed environments is encrypted.
- Certificates and secrets are managed using standard secret management practices; access is restricted by role-based controls.

What we do not claim (customer-facing)
- We do not describe the system as “end-to-end encrypted” or “zero-knowledge,” because Redwood must decrypt traffic within the serving environment to process requests.

2) Encryption at rest
Hosted API
- Data stored in Redwood-managed systems is encrypted at rest using cloud-provider encryption capabilities.
- Backups/snapshots for supported storage systems are encrypted.

Dedicated
- Customer data in Dedicated deployments is encrypted at rest in the Redwood-managed environment, using cloud-provider encryption capabilities.
- Dedicated is designed to provide stronger isolation boundaries than multi-tenant Hosted (e.g., reserved capacity and tenant separation).

Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Private deployments are designed to run in customer-controlled environments.
- At-rest encryption is enabled using the customer’s chosen infrastructure controls (e.g., their cloud storage encryption settings, database encryption, and backup policies).

Notes / common customer questions
- Ephemeral processing: Models and request data may be processed in memory during inference; at-rest encryption does not apply to transient memory.
- Caches: Depending on configuration (e.g., performance caching), some data may be stored temporarily to improve throughput/latency. Cache behavior and retention are addressed in the Data Retention & Deletion Overview.

3) Key management (KMS/HSM) by deployment mode
Key principles (customer-facing)
- Keys are stored and managed using industry-standard key management services.
- Access to keys is restricted to authorized systems and personnel under least-privilege principles.
- Key rotation and lifecycle management follow defined internal procedures.

Hosted API (Redwood-managed keys)
- Encryption keys for Hosted environments are managed by Redwood using cloud-provider KMS capabilities.
- Customers seeking customer-managed keys (BYOK/CMK) or specific HSM requirements should typically evaluate Dedicated or Private, depending on the control requirements.

Dedicated (Redwood-managed keys; enhanced options may be available)
- Dedicated environments use Redwood-managed encryption keys backed by cloud-provider KMS.
- For advanced requirements (e.g., customer-managed keys or customer-controlled key policies), Redwood may support design patterns depending on the customer’s architecture and selected cloud/region; confirm availability through Solutions Engineering and Security/GRC during the security review.

Private (Customer-managed keys)
- In Private deployments, customers can manage encryption keys within their own environment using their chosen KMS.
- Customers can enforce their own key rotation policies, separation of duties, and key access workflows.
- If the customer uses a cloud-provider KMS that is backed by HSM, the customer’s encryption keys benefit from those HSM-backed controls as provided by their cloud vendor.
- For on-prem deployments, customers can integrate with their preferred key management and HSM solutions subject to deployment architecture.

Key ownership boundaries (customer-facing)
- Hosted: Redwood is responsible for key management operations within the Hosted environment.
- Dedicated: Redwood is responsible for key management operations within the Dedicated environment, with potential customer-specific enhancements by agreement.
- Private: The customer is responsible for key management operations in their environment.

4) Audit logging and audit evidence tie-ins
Operational audit logging (Redwood Console / platform)
- Redwood provides audit logging for security-relevant actions (e.g., authentication events and administrative/configuration changes) as supported by the product and customer plan.
- Audit log exports and retention options may vary by plan and deployment mode.

Key management audit trails
- Hosted/Dedicated: Underlying KMS activity logging is managed within Redwood’s cloud accounts; evidence can be provided through the standard evidence request process under NDA, as applicable.
- Private: Customers can rely on their cloud provider’s KMS audit logs (e.g., key usage and administrative events) within their own accounts, in addition to Redwood platform audit logs.

How to request evidence (internal note)
- SOC 2 report and related evidence is available via the SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook (NDA required). Do not attach reports over email.

5) Deployment mode comparison (customer-facing quick table)
Hosted API
- In transit: TLS for API/Console.
- At rest: Encrypted at rest in Redwood-managed storage.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood-managed KMS.
- Audit tie-ins: Redwood audit logs (feature/retention depends on plan) + evidence via NDA.

Dedicated
- In transit: TLS for API/Console; customer-specific networking options.
- At rest: Encrypted at rest in Redwood-managed storage.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood-managed KMS; customer-specific key requirements may be supported by agreement.
- Audit tie-ins: Redwood audit logs + evidence via NDA; integration options may be configured per customer.

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- In transit: Encrypted transport; can be constrained to private networking.
- At rest: Encrypted using customer-controlled infrastructure settings.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Audit tie-ins: Customer’s KMS logs in their account + Redwood audit logs for platform actions.

6) Approved phrasing (copy/paste blocks for questionnaires)
Encryption in transit
“Redwood Inference uses TLS to protect customer traffic to the API and console. Internal service-to-service traffic is also encrypted. Redwood follows modern best practices for TLS configuration and periodically reviews cipher suites and protocol versions.”

Encryption at rest
“Customer data stored in Redwood-managed environments is encrypted at rest using cloud-provider encryption capabilities. For Private deployments, customers control storage encryption and key management within their environment.”

Key management / customer-managed keys
“Hosted deployments use Redwood-managed encryption keys backed by cloud-provider KMS. Private deployments support customer-managed keys via the customer’s KMS/HSM controls. For Dedicated deployments, advanced key management requirements can be reviewed with Redwood during the security review to determine supported options for the specific deployment architecture.”

7) Do-not-say / guardrails (internal)
- Do not claim: “end-to-end encryption,” “zero knowledge,” or “customer holds the only keys” (unless Private and explicitly true for that customer’s deployment).
- Do not claim: “HSM” unless we specify “cloud-provider KMS backed by HSM” or the customer’s own HSM in Private.
- Do not hard-code crypto algorithm claims (e.g., “AES-256 everywhere”) unless Security Engineering has explicitly approved the wording for all storage layers in scope.

Open questions for reviewers (internal)
1) Hosted/Dedicated: confirm the strongest customer-facing statement we can make about backups/snapshots encryption scope.
2) Dedicated: clarify whether we want to offer a standardized statement for CMK/BYOK as “available by agreement” vs “not currently supported.” (Naomi + Marcus to align with product behavior; avoid ambiguity.)
3) Audit logs: confirm which audit log event categories we want to reference in a one-pager without creating a feature promise (tie to current audit logging overview).

Review + next steps (internal)

- GRC review: Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter

Last updated (internal)
2026-02-26 (OP): Incorporated field feedback on KMS/HSM phrasing; added stronger guardrails on “end-to-end” language; clarified Private = customer-controlled key management.
